technology_platform.name: IL-2 Superkine fused to recombinant human albumin scaffold
design_features: Beta-Enhanced Not-Alpha IL-2: Preferentially activates CD122 (IL-2 receptor beta)
No CD25 Binding: Minimal/no stimulation of immunosuppressive Tregs
Seven Specific Mutations: Engineered for optimal immune effector cell activation
Albumin Fusion: Improved PK, enhanced tumor accumulation, natural accumulation in tumor-draining lymph nodes
Target Cells: Preferentially activates CD8+ T cells and NK cells

safety_summary.dose_limiting_toxicities: None at doses up to 120 µg/kg
safety_summary.grade_3_4_events: Mainly laboratory abnormalities without clinical sequelae

survival_analysis.key_finding: Tumor control (CR, PR, or SD) was significantly associated with prolonged overall survival in both monotherapy and combination cohorts

clinical_implications: Differentiated Mechanism: Stands out from other next-generation IL-2s with consistent anti-tumor activity
Checkpoint Inhibitor Refractory Activity: 42% ORR in post-ICI patients across tumor types; 38% ORR in checkpoint-resistant melanoma
Demonstrates activity where standard therapies fail
Durable Responses: Long-term remissions observed in melanoma (>7 months) and pancreatic MSI-H (>21 months)
Broad Anti-Tumor Activity: Responses in multiple difficult-to-treat cancers
Superior to ORR Benchmarks: Exceeds objective response rate benchmarks in difficult-to-treat populations
Earlier Line Potential: Strong activity in immediate post-ICI setting suggests potential for earlier treatment lines
Survival Benefit: Disease control significantly associated with prolonged OS (HR ~0.28-0.29)
Combination Synergy: MDNA11 + pembrolizumab shows activity in primary ICI-resistant disease
Excellent Tolerability: >90% Grade 1-2 events, transient side effects

NEO_CYT_trial.rationale: Healthier immune systems in earlier-stage patients

Additional data updates expected in coming weeks/months
